summary: Submitted a second-scenario check for the already-confirmed requirement c-verify-leader-voter-quorum, with preflight returning valid:true. Rationale: the first scenario used a configuration with a single non-voter and its own limitations recorded that configurations with several non-voters were unexercised, so this artifact fixes that layout while leaving the requirement, oracle, binding and unit unchanged - which is why no new claim, candidate or binding was submitted and the product is a plain check selecting unit-c-verify-leader-voter-quorum with plan check-plan-verify-two.json and harness check-harness-verify-two.go. Harness: a five-server configuration with voters n1, n2, n3 and non-voters n4, n5 elects a leader, the leader's routes to both other voters are removed with the transport's own Disconnect while the two non-voters keep answering, and the leader then calls VerifyLeader; local execution emitted verification_setup (leader n2, voters 3, nonvoters 2, quorum_size 2, non_voters n4,n5, leader_state Leader) and verification_observed with other_voter_reachable false, verification_result success, empty error, leader_state Leader and leader_stats_state Leader, so the leader confirmed itself on its own vote plus two non-voter acknowledgements against a voter majority of two, which no arithmetical coincidence of a single non-voter can explain. Plan: claim c-verify-leader-voter-quorum, binding bind-raft-verify-leader-quorum, admission alias admit on verification_setup, monitor on verification_observed with applicability requiring voters 3, nonvoters 2, quorum_size 2 and an unreachable voter, and the property verification_result ne success with identity cluster/op; limitations kept explicit (the observable is the outcome not a downstream stale read, an unfinished verification is not distinguished from a failure, and mixed reachable-voter/reachable-non-voter layouts are not exercised). If the runner executes this before the deadline the next turn should review it to lift the unreviewed-correspondence blocker on this second witness.
